answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token deposit before it may submit jobs or vote, then slash that deposit when independently audited behavior proves fraud, such as claiming payment for a task it never completed. One person can still create many identities, but each must tie up capital, and coordinated cheating risks losing it; Sybil resistance comes from making influence costly, not from pretending identities are unique. An ivory marketplace might price deposits dynamically as a comet of new accounts arrives, while ensuring honest newcomers can still begin a voyage.
